>Just because you like some aspects of technologies doesn't mean they 
>are good.  Nor that people's fears about them were "irrational".  
>Telephones invade people's privacy plenty.  People's attitudes towards
>cars as crude invaders that were going to destroy civilized life were

>Yes, the Old Order Amish don't use electricity.

Nick, what's so silly about this discussion? And, believe it or not, there are
plenty of Amish who use more technology than we "English" would know about,
except for people who live near them. I find that interesting, not as a
pro-tech argument either. That could go either way, but perhaps counters TK's
argument that the bad parts of technology cannot be separated from the good
parts.

True enough, just because I like some aspects of some technologies doesn't mean
that they are good. I have never considered myself the final arbiter on this
issue. But, just because you don't like certain technologies doesn't mean they
are bad either.

Don't you think that any of this is worth talking about? Or do you prefer to
dismiss the opinions of those you disagree with?
